title: Influence of the dietary supplement taurine on the cardiovascular system in chronic heart failure
summary: In this study, the potential effects of taurine, an freely available dietary supplement, on the severity and progression of heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) will be investigated. The focus is on possible changes in cardiovascular function and blood glucose metabolism, which are investigated using state-of-the-art methods.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Disease definition according to established guidelines: HFpEF is defined as a sign and symptom of heart failure with a left ventricular ejection fraction of ≥50%
Exclusion criteria:
- Declined participation in the study
- Inability to provide informed consent
- Life expectancy < 1 year
- History of heart failure with reduced systolic function (HFrEF) (exception: acute heart failure only)
- End-stage renal disease or requirement for dialysis
- Myocardial infarction (ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction [STEMI] or non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction [NSTEMI]) and/or urgent or elective percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) within the previous 30 days
- Cardiac surgery within the previous 3 months
- Alternative cardiac diagnoses that, in the opinion of the investigator, could account for the patient's heart failure symptoms, including severe right-sided heart failure in the absence of left ventricular structural abnormalities; specific etiologies such as infiltrative cardiomyopathy, genetic hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, constrictive pericarditis, cardiac sarcoidosis, cardiac amyloidosis, other storage diseases, clinically significant congenital heart disease, or severe valvular heart disease requiring surgical or transcatheter intervention
- Alternative non-cardiac diagnoses that, in the opinion of the investigator, could account for the patient's heart failure symptoms, including severe pulmonary disease (e.g., pulmonary arterial hypertension or severe chronic obstructive pulmonary disease [COPD], GOLD stage >2) or severe anemia (hemoglobin <10 g/dL in men or <9.5 g/dL in women)
- Taurine supplementation within the previous 3 months
